title: Mashbooh
subtitle: Ingredient of uncertain origin under Islamic Law.
description: BOTIA signals when the halal status cannot be confirmed from the label alone.
why_body: Under Islamic Law, food additives derived from unlawful sources are also unlawful (Codex CAC/GL 24-1997). However, food labels worldwide do not require declaring the origin of many ingredients — flavourings, emulsifiers, enzymes, and gelatins may come from animal, plant, or alcohol-based sources without this being visible on the label.
what_body: Ingredient detected whose halal status cannot be confirmed from the label alone. See BOTIA Note below for details.
can_1: Detect when an ingredient's halal status is not declared on the label.
can_2: Flag that the origin may be animal, plant, or alcohol-based.
can_3: Inform you that the decision belongs to you and your religious authority.
cannot_1: Confirm or deny halal status of any ingredient.
cannot_2: Determine the actual origin of the ingredient from the label.
cannot_3: Replace the judgment of a qualified religious authority.
closing: BOTIA signals that the origin is undeclared — the decision belongs to you and your religious authority.
